facts.statement: The holotype of Peirosaurus was collected by Llewellyn Ivor Price between 1947 and 1949 from the Serra da Galga Formation in Brazil, dating to approximately 68 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected by Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1947-1949 at the Price Quarry 3, Peirópolis Site near Uberaba, in the Serra da Galga Formation (Bauru Group), dating to the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 68-66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Peirosaurus is known from a fragmentary holotype skull containing five teeth and a partial postcranial skeleton including ribs and dermal plates.
facts.quote: Peirosaurus is known from the holotype DGM 433-R, fragmentary skull (left premaxilla bearing five teeth, isolated maxillary and dentary teeth and left palpebral bone) and partial postcranial skeleton including radius, ulna, left pubis and ischium, some presacral and a single caudal vertebrae, ribs, haemal arches and dermal plates.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that traits previously used to link Peirosaurus with Argentine material are actually shared with other peirosaurids and mesoeucrocodylians.
facts.quote: However, more recently Agustín G. Martinelli, Joseph J.W. Sertich, Alberto C. Garrido and Ángel M. Praderio concluded that the traits which used to unite the holotype (from Brazil) and the referred material from Argentina are shared with other peirosaurids and some other mesoeucrocodylians.

facts.statement: Following the reassignment of Argentine specimens to the new genus Gasparinisuchus, Peirosaurus is known only from its single holotype.
facts.quote: Hence, Peirosaurus is known only from its holotype.

facts.statement: The rostrum of Peirosaurus was laterally compressed with a groove between the maxilla and premaxilla designed to accommodate an enlarged mandibular tooth.
facts.quote: The rostrum is laterally compressed with a grove between the maxilla and premaxilla to accommodate for an enlarged mandibular tooth.

facts.statement: Peirosaurus had thin dorsal osteoderms with low longitudinal keels and smaller abdominal osteoderms that lacked keels.
facts.quote: The dorsal osteoderms are thin and sculptured with low longitudinal keels while the abdominal ones are smaller and lack keels.

facts.statement: Peirosaurus possessed a wedge-like anterior process on the maxilla.
facts.quote: A maxillary wedge-like anterior process is also present.

facts.statement: The external nares of Peirosaurus faced slightly forward and protruded anteriorly.
facts.quote: The external nares face slightly forward and anteriorly protrude.

facts.statement: Peirosaurus is the type genus of the family Peirosauridae and contains the single species Peirosaurus torminni.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Peirosaurus torminni. It is the type genus of the family Peirosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus Peirosaurus was described by Price in 1955.
facts.quote: authority: Price, 1955

facts.statement: Peirosaurus lived during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Minas Gerais, southern Brazil.
facts.quote: Peirosaurus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid crocodylomorph known from the Late Cretaceous period (late Maastrichtian stage) of Minas Gerais, southern Brazil.

facts.statement: It is debated whether minor differences in osteoderm thickness and tooth carinae have sufficient taxonomic value to distinguish Peirosaurus from Uberabasuchus.
facts.quote: However, these characters are considered to be minor and their taxonomic value may be individually variable.

facts.statement: Several features of the premaxilla and dentition of Peirosaurus are shared exclusively with the closely related genus Uberabasuchus.
facts.quote: Though many of the features of the premaxilla and dentition of Peirosaurus are widespread among peirosaurids and many mesoeucrocodylians, several are shared exclusively with Uberabasuchus.

facts.statement: The genus Peirosaurus was named by Price in 1955.

facts.statement: Peirosaurus is a member of the class Reptilia.
